Ingredients:

Marinara Sauce

  • 2 teaspoons extra-virgin olive oil
  • 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 cups chopped plum tomatoes, with juices
  • 6 oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, drained and finely chopped
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground pepper
  • 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil

Burgers

  • 1 pound 93%-lean ground turkey
  • 1/4 cup finely chopped scallions
  • 2 teaspoons minced garlic
  • 2 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce
  • 1 teaspoon freshly grated lemon zest
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground pepper
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup shredded part-skim mozzarella cheese, divided
  • 2 tablespoons finely chopped fresh basil
  • 2 teaspoons extra-virgin olive oil
  • 4 4-inch-square slices foccacia bread, toasted

Directions:

  1. To prepare marinara: Heat 2 teaspoons oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add onion and garlic, cover and cook, stirring frequently, until translucent, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir in fresh tomatoes and any juices, sun-dried tomatoes, 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/2 teaspoon pepper. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down, 8 to 10 minutes. Stir in basil and remove from the heat. Transfer to a food processor and pulse to form a coarse-textured sauce. Return to the pan and set aside.
  2. To prepare burgers: Place turkey, scallions, garlic, Worcestershire sauce, lemon zest, oregano, 1/2 teaspoon pepper and 1/4 teaspoon salt in a large bowl. Gently combine, without overmixing, until evenly incorporated. Form into 8 thin patties about 4 inches wide and 3/8 inch thick.
  3. Combine 1/4 cup cheese and basil and place an equal amount in the center of 4 patties. Cover with the remaining patties and crimp the edges closed.
  4. Heat 2 teaspoons oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add burgers and cook, turning once, until an instant-read thermometer inserted in the center registers 165°F, 8 to 10 minutes total.
  5. Warm the marinara on the stove. To assemble the burgers, spread 3 tablespoons of marinara on each toasted bread, top with a burger, about 3 more tablespoons of marinara and 1 tablespoon of the remaining cheese.

Nutrition Facts per Serving:

  • 299 calories
  • 15 g fat
  • 74 mg cholesterol
  • 14 g carbohydrates
  • 28 g protein
  • 2 g fiber
  • 706 mg sodium

I'd like to collect opinions on NSFW posts now that a tag has been implemented by Voat.

The mods will post an official thread on this later, this is merely to collect community opinion.

** DO NOT POST NSFW until mods decide on more rules concerning it. **

EDIT: There was a false rumor, but we do still want opinions.
I definitely prefer no nsfw posts during the week. Maybe lightly nsfw things during shitpost sunday, but no hentai levels of nsfw.

I don't think NSFW as a whole should be banned. Essentially as someone who keeps posting discussions, I think having more 'mature themed' discussions that take a look at specific subjects would be pretty interesting. Designating the post as NSFW would allow people to bring up examples and topics without worry and I think that's pretty neat. (Also, doesn't look like /v/hentai is a place that would be friendly to that kind of posting.) I am not saying I'd be posting discussions about porn, but topics that may or may not touch sensitive subjects (twss?).

Overall, stuff like simple images and videos that are low effort are essentially porn, and porn has its place (I don't think /v/anime is it). Also, since NSFW stands for 'Not Safe For Work' I think that adding the tag to things such as extreme violence might be good - unless people think it's too confusing.

EDIT: Anime with heavy nudity or actual (not implied or hidden) sex will need to be approved on a case-by-case basis by mods. For example, straight up hentai with no plot to discuss? No. Something like Mardock Scramble that has sex but a real plotline? Perhaps.

(Again, because I don't think discussions are received well on hentai boards in general.)

I raise the flag of Elfen Lied. Posting clips, images, or even discussions of the moral and ethical issues within the show would all be very much so not safe for work. A lot of employers don't care to have workers talking about genetic superiority, genocides, slavery, and forced sterilization. All of which are topics that are both germane and appropriate to any discussion of the themes of Elfen Lied.

The same would be true of any discussion surrounding interesting cultural quirks. Why are underpants so fetishized in Japan, and what does that have to do with modern day fan service? (The answer is that when underwear was first introduced to Japan, it was first used by escorts and prostitutes. The stigma of sexuality stuck even after it became mainstream. This is why panty shots are so ubiquitous as a fan service). Right now we can discuss it in text, but linking to actual articles would be against the rules -- even if they would be educational.

So in short: I agree with your stance. If for some reason we need sanity, we could have a NSFW Saturday (which would be useful since Saturday is typically associated with being a day off from work/school).

As long as there is a line drawn between ecchi and hentai, I don't think NSFW posts should be banned if they are tagged properly.

Plus(and this is my most important point), there is an option in settings to turn off NSFW content. So why can't the people who are complaining just uncheck the 'Display NSFW content' box?
